query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: problem_domain
per_column.rationale: Derived from short_description/category, this categorizes the issue type. It is known at intake, lies outside resolution_time, and different domains plausibly differ in how long they take to resolve.

per_column.name: incident_severity_urgency
per_column.rationale: Captures severity/urgency (system_down vs informational), knowable early and independent of resolution_time; a plausible driver of resolution duration.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: System-wide vs user-level scope is available at intake and outside the focus; broader scope plausibly correlates with longer resolution.

per_column.name: resolution_ownership_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Framed around 'resolution' ownership mismatch, this is likely derived from closure/reassignment fields that are only settled once the incident is being/has been resolved, so it risks encoding post-outcome information rather than a pre-resolution signal.

per_column.name: technical_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Complexity/technology category is knowable from the description at intake, sits outside the focus, and complexity plausibly predicts resolution duration.

per_column.name: responder_expertise_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Whether a domain expert vs generalist is assigned (and escalation need) is largely determinable at assignment time, is distinct from resolution_time, and expertise mismatch plausibly lengthens resolution. Escalation_required carries mild leakage risk but overall functions as a predictor.

per_column.name: incident_closure_status
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is closed vs open is a direct function of the outcome; resolution_time is only well-defined/measurable for closed incidents, so this restates/leaks the outcome rather than predicting it.

judge.rationale: Five columns (problem_domain, incident_severity_urgency, scope_indicator, technical_complexity_signal, responder_expertise_mismatch) are legitimate, intake- or assignment-time predictors that add genuine signal beyond the raw fields for modeling resolution_time. Two columns fail: incident_closure_status directly encodes the outcome (leakage/restatement), and resolution_ownership_mismatch is defined around the resolution process and likely encodes post-outcome information. The valid set provides moderate-to-good leverage, but some features are partly redundant with existing priority/category columns and two clear leakage columns lower the overall quality.
